word:lxx:L701051.explanation: This verb means to dig up or turn over the ground. In the Greek Old Testament, it describes an action of excavating earth rather than a feeling, quality, or title. It points to a very young child dependent on breast-feeding, rather than to an older child or adult. The word appears once in the Greek Old Testament translation corpus, in 3 Maccabees 3:27. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is a suckling child or one under the breast.

word:lxx:L713254.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means to “bring to light from under”—to reveal or make something visible when it has been beneath or hidden. It describes an action rather than a person, object, or quality. The word occurs twice in the Greek LXX, both times in 2 Maccabees. Its exact force in either passage depends on what is being brought into view and the surrounding sentence.

word:lxx:L713283.explanation: This verb means “carry the neck high; show off,” describing someone who presents himself in a visibly proud, self-important way. It focuses on outward bearing or display rather than simply identifying an inward feeling. The word occurs twice in the Greek LXX, once in 2 Maccabees and once in 3 Maccabees. Its precise force in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and context.

word:lxx:L713504.explanation: This verb describes having a friendly disposition and a kindly mind toward someone. It expresses a warm, considerate attitude directed at another person, rather than merely naming friendliness as an abstract quality. In the Greek LXX corpus represented here, it occurs once, in 2 Maccabees 2:25. Its precise force in that sentence depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic idea is to regard or treat someone with kindness and goodwill.

word:lxx:L713548.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “murder” or “deed of murder,” referring to the act of unlawfully killing someone. It names the killing itself rather than a person who commits it. The word occurs once in the Greek LXX corpus, in 1 Maccabees 1:24. Its precise force in that passage depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but its basic meaning remains a deed involving murder.

word:lxx:L713643.explanation: This noun means a “light source” or “beacon”: something that gives or displays light. In the Greek Old Testament and related Greek writings, it refers to lights in the heavens and other shining bodies. The word occurs seven times in this Greek corpus, beginning in Genesis and appearing also in Daniel, Wisdom, and Sirach. Its basic sense remains focused on a visible source of light rather than light considered only as an abstract idea.

word:lxx:L713694.explanation: This noun means “bronze-worker” or “copper-shaper”: a person who makes or forms objects from bronze or copper. It identifies someone by skilled work with metal rather than describing the metal itself. The word occurs once in the Greek LXX, in Wisdom 15:9. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its ordinary meaning remains a craftsman who shapes bronze or copper.

word:lxx:L713711.explanation: The word is a proper name, given in the lexical sense as “Chananaios; Khananeos.” It functions as a designation rather than an ordinary action, quality, or object-word. In the Greek Old Testament, it occurs 69 times, from Genesis through Zechariah, so it is used repeatedly across the Old Testament Greek corpus. Its exact referent in any particular passage must be determined from that passage’s surrounding text; the word itself supplies the name, not the full situation or significance.

word:lxx:L713870.explanation: Chiōn means snow.‡ It is also used in comparisons for something white as snow.

word:lxx:L713957.explanation: This noun means “goodness of heart” or “generosity of spirit.” It describes an inward disposition marked by kindness, benevolence, and a willing concern for others. The word names a quality of character rather than a single outward action. In the Greek LXX corpus represented here, it occurs once, in Sirach 37:11; the precise force of that occurrence depends on its surrounding passage. Its central idea remains a generous and kindly spirit toward others.

word:lxx:L714071.explanation: This adjective describes something “soulish; psychological”—that is, something related to the soul or inner psychological life. It identifies the kind of thing being discussed rather than naming an action. In the Greek LXX corpus represented here, it occurs once, in 4 Maccabees 1:32. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording, but its basic meaning points to the inward, soul-related or psychological aspect of a person or matter.

word:lxx:L714134.explanation: This word describes something as beautiful—pleasing in appearance and worthy of admiration. It functions as a verb in the Greek Old Testament, expressing the quality of being beautiful rather than naming a person or object itself. In the surviving Greek Old Testament occurrences, it appears twice, both in Song of Songs, where it is rendered “beautiful.” Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding wording, but its central meaning remains the expression of beauty.
